idiom_name: std::sync::mpsc (or tokio mpsc) inbox + one owner task
implementation_notes: The idiomatic Rust mediator is a task that owns the shared state and receives events on a channel: colleagues get a Sender clone and send messages, the hub task receives and routes to the other colleagues' senders, and no aliased mutable object graph is needed. std::sync::mpsc provides multi-producer/single-consumer FIFO communication with send/recv, so many colleagues can publish while exactly one hub consumes; the Go-style single-owner monitor in the standard library's codewalk describes the same shape. This is the realization to reach for first in Rust - sending moves ownership, so there is no data race to guard, and the borrow checker is not fought.
pitfalls: mpsc is multi-producer/single-consumer: exactly one task may own the Receiver, so several consumers need crossbeam-channel, tokio's broadcast, or explicit fan-out from the hub task.
An unbounded channel lets a slow hub grow memory without limit; prefer a bounded capacity (tokio::sync::mpsc::channel(n)) and decide the full policy (await vs try_send vs drop).
When every Sender is dropped the channel closes and the hub loop exits silently; keep a Sender alive in the hub or handle the disconnect error.
Sending moves the value, so senders cannot reuse the payload, and large messages should travel as Arc<T> rather than copies.

variants.name: Rc<RefCell> object-graph mediator (classic structure)
variants.implementation_notes: The classic object graph is possible but hand-written: the hub is Rc<RefCell<..>> (Arc<Mutex<..>> across threads), colleagues are Rc<RefCell<dyn Colleague>> trait objects, and notify borrows the hub mutably through RefCell. Choose it only for small, single-threaded, GUI-like graphs where messages would be awkward and participants are genuinely shared - and hold the back-reference from colleague to hub as Weak so the graph cannot cycle. This is the realization the borrow checker pushes against; the channel variant is usually the better answer.
pitfalls: Rc<RefCell> reference cycles never free: a colleague storing a strong Rc back to the hub leaks the whole graph, so use Weak for the back-reference.
RefCell borrows are checked at runtime: borrow_mut() while another borrow is active panics (and the Mutex equivalent deadlocks), which makes a handler that re-enters the hub a real hazard.
Rc/RefCell is neither Send nor Sync; sharing the hub across threads requires Arc<Mutex<..>> or Arc<RwLock<..>> and changes the design.
Every dispatch is a dynamic call through dyn Colleague behind a runtime borrow check, which costs ergonomics and some performance the channel variant avoids.
